File: README.md

Argus V2: ink detection on native 9 µm scans

Weights: https://huggingface.co/ruiconte/argus-v2 (argus-v2.pth, MIT). Argus V1 card below.

Argus V2 is Reader V3 fine-tuned on native 8–9 µm scans, the kind of scan the unread scrolls have. It uses the same network and file layout as reader-v3.pth, so it is a drop-in replacement: HerculeX, ink-sdk or any tool that loads Reader V3 loads Argus V2 unchanged.

V1 was trained on renders pooled from 2.4 µm scans. It was strong on that format, but on native 113 keV scans it lost to Reader V3 (PHerc0841 AUC 0.869 vs 0.913), as pointed out on Discord. V2 fixes this.

All numbers use 256 px tiles and 8-fold test-time augmentation for both models, run through the same code. The threshold for "background marked as ink" is each model's own 80 % recall threshold.

Where Argus V2 is weaker

On PHerc1447 w058 its AUC is 0.2 points below Reader V3, although Dice, bAcc and background are better there. On the three official validation masks (pooled renders), Argus V1 is still the better model, and Reader V3 is slightly ahead of V2. For pooled 2.4 µm renders of those scrolls, use V1. For native scans, use V2.

Native 113 keV render of PHerc0841, which no model here was trained on: Reader V3, Argus V2, Argus V2 with the layer order reversed, team labels.

PHerc1447 w060, native 116 keV: the same four panels.

Other tools: load it exactly like reader-v3.pth, with a 17-layer window centred on the surface and robust MAD normalisation. Depth windows: averaging three windows shifted by −2, 0 and +2 layers adds about one AUC point to both models. On native 0841: Argus V2 0.928, Reader V3 0.922.

Start: domenicor046/reader-v3 (MIT). Fine-tune: 12 000 iterations on 256 px tiles, batch 8, SGD at learning rate 2.5e-4, BCE with label smoothing 0.5 plus Dice. The depth order is never flipped during training. Data: a random 30 % share, in blocks, of the supervised area of the 70 native segments in

domenicor046/reader-v2-labels (MIT), with the public native surface volumes. These cover PHerc0139, 0814 and 0500P2 at 113 keV, PHerc0009B and 0343P at 116 keV, and PHerc0172 at 53 keV. Checkpoint selection: three held-out native segments from those labels (0139 w050, 0009B 20250511200236 and 0814 20250925212701). Never used for training or selection: PHerc0841 and PHerc1447. Code: native_v2_prep.py, train.py and seg_eval.py in https://github.com/ruiconte/ink-swarm.

Reader V3 and reader-v2-labels: domenicor046. The ink_9um network: the Vesuvius Challenge team. PHerc1447 test labels: YoussefMoNader (CC BY-NC 4.0, used for evaluation only).

Scan data: Vesuvius Challenge open data.

Argus V1: ink detection for the Herculaneum scrolls

Weights: https://huggingface.co/ruiconte/argus-v1 (argus-v1.pth, MIT)

Argus V1 is a drop-in ink checkpoint for 9 µm-scale surface volumes. It uses the same network as

scrollprize/ink_9um and Reader V3 (vesuvius_unet_3d_stem_2d, 17-layer window, 34.6 M parameters) and the same file layout as reader-v3.pth, so any tool that loads Reader V3 loads Argus V1 unchanged.

All numbers use 256 px tiles and 8-fold test-time augmentation. Every model is run through the same code.

Reader V3 was trained on native 113/116 keV scans. These masks use the 2.4 µm-derived volumes, so this table favours models trained on that format. Read the PHerc0841 table first.

Where Argus is weaker

On PHerc0841, Reader V3 still has a slightly better Dice (0.767 vs 0.758) and marks slightly less background as ink (8.5 % vs 8.9 %).

Argus marks more of the papyrus as ink than Reader V3. On PHerc0139 w053 at the same 80 % recall it flags 14.9 % of a central 3072 px crop, against 10.0 % for Reader V3. That crop is not blank. The team's 1 µm-scan map shows a line of letters inside it. When the depth order is reversed, Argus's marks in the crop fall from 14.9 % to 1.1 % (Reader V3's from 10.0 % to 2.7 %). Pixels the team map calls blank. Restricted to those pixels: forward: Argus flags 10.3 % (Reader V3 6.9 %); reversed: Argus flags 1.0 % (Reader V3 2.7 %). Inner wrap w057. On a central crop, Argus flags 8.9 % forward and 1.5 % reversed; Reader V3 flags 4.7 % and 2.2 %. Ink the team map sees. Argus finds 80 % of it on w053, Reader V3 61 %. How to read this. The extra marks depend on the physical depth direction. They look like faint ink, not like texture hallucination, but there are no human labels there to prove it. Treat them as leads to check, not as readings.

PHerc0139 w053, central crop: CT, Reader V3, Argus V1, and Argus V1 with the layer order reversed.

Never-seen PHerc0841: Reader V3, Argus V1, Argus V1 reversed, human labels.

Other tools: anything that reads reader-v3.pth can read this file: it holds the same model keys and a config dict. Use a 17-layer window centred on the surface, robust MAD normalisation (1-99 %), and 256 px tiles or larger. Larger inference tiles helped every model we tested.

Base: domenicor046/ink9um-dense dense9um-all7-step075000.pth (MIT). Fine-tunes: 8 runs of 8 000 iterations each. Tiles: 256 px, batch 8. Learning rate: 2.5e-4 or 5e-4, 4 seeds each. Labels: dense pseudo-labels from domenicor046/ink9um-dense. Loss: BCE with label smoothing 0.5, plus Dice. Data: PHerc0139, PHerc1667, PHerc Paris 4 and PHerc0814 surface volumes from the Vesuvius Challenge open data. Depth flip removed. Unlike the reference recipe, the depth order is never flipped during training. With the flip, the model ignored the physical depth direction: reversed-order AUC was 0.79. Without it, reversed-order AUC is 0.53. Weight soup. The 8 fine-tunes share one initialisation and are averaged into one set of weights (Wortsman et al., 2022). The soup beats every single run on the validation masks. Held out: the validation masks above, all of PHerc0841, and PHerc0139 w053 were never used for training or model selection.

Reproduce the numbers

pip install torch numpy zarr numcodecs scipy pillow requests safetensors python prep.py # training / validation surface volumes (2.4 um, level 2, 21 pooled layers) python dense_prep.py # dense labels from domenicor046/ink9um-dense python heldout_prep.py # never-seen PHerc0841 w00 + PHerc0139 w053 in the same format python eval_all.py # fetches the public checkpoints compared here python heldout_eval.py --patch 256 --tta 8 # PHerc0841 table + w053 + reversed-order control python val256.py argus-v1.pth official/reader-v3.pth # validation-mask table

Training: train.py --arch official --labels dense --iters 8000 --warmup 500 --patch 256 --batch 8

--init official/dense-all7-75k.pth --lr {2.5e-4|5e-4} --seed {1..4} --zflip 0, then soup.py --match

<prefix>.

Built on the ink_9um network and recipe (Vesuvius Challenge team). Uses the dense labels and checkpoints of domenicor046 (ink9um-dense; Reader V2/V3 for comparison). Compared against Nieuwlaar's ink9um-dense-native. All of these are MIT-licensed. Scan data: Vesuvius Challenge open data, under its own terms.
